components.name: Home calls stopped panel
components.description: Schematic documentation preview, not the actual native implementation. One positive historical Action panel shows Calls stopped, a large numeral, Last 7 days, and See calls; the full panel opens the held filter. The existing API aggregate includes held and verification over rolling seven days, never all confirmed scams or a lifetime total. Native source uses title3.bold(), largeTitle.scaled(by: 1.5).bold() with monospaced digits, adaptive actionInk, and a native list-row background. Zero instead uses a neutral surface and None in the last 7 days; unavailable data is not zero. Real status stays above this historical panel. Source: Features/Overview/StoppedCallsCard.swift, Features/Overview/OverviewView.swift, and backend/src/cloud/api.ts. narrative.overview:
Shield keeps a familiar native iPhone appearance: grouped lists, straightforward labels, system text, and recognizable controls. Quiet surfaces and four adaptive accents help people find a call, understand its result, and choose the next action. The library metaphor describes legible wayfinding; it does not introduce themed decoration.

The October 12 refinement makes an 80-year-old's understanding the bar. Ordinary screens use everyday words, fewer visible choices, and room for text to grow. Less common details open on request. Setup, disconnection, privacy, and sharing retain the information and explicit confirmations needed for a meaningful choice.
keyCharacteristics: Native tabs, navigation stacks, grouped lists, forms, sheets, menus, and confirmation dialogs.
Action blue, stopped-call red, answered-call teal, and voicemail violet with Light, Dark, and increased-contrast variants.
Semantic Dynamic Type, wrapping text, generous app controls, and content-based stacking.
Explicit person context, sharing scope, truthful service state, and a persistent sample-data marker.

rules.name: The Outcome Truth Rule
rules.body: Pair color with a familiar outcome label or symbol; a call being checked, offered, or answered never implies an authenticated caller.

rules.name: The Native Type Rule
rules.body: Preserve semantic text styles and allow wrapping or stacking before introducing a fixed text size.

rules.name: The Native Surface Rule
rules.body: Use grouped system surfaces and native control feedback before introducing custom elevation or viewport geometry.

rules.name: The Historical Count Rule
rules.body: Label the seven-day scope, include review-needed calls honestly, and keep historical activity distinct from current protection status; unavailable data is never zero.

rules.name: The Visible Context Rule
rules.body: Show the viewed person and sharing scope in words, and keep participant ownership distinct from helper access.

dos: Do use ShieldTheme's adaptive role colors, opaque supporting text, and native grouped system surfaces.
Do pair outcome color with familiar words and SF Symbols while preserving uncertainty.
Do keep semantic Dynamic Type, wrapping text, content-based stacking, 52-point shared app action minima, and 60-point grouped-row defaults.
Do give ordinary tasks one clear next action and reveal less common detail on request.
Do make person context, voicemail permission, and sample-only state visible in words.
Do retain explicit privacy, sharing, setup, and disconnection confirmations.
Do label the Home count as rolling seven-day historical activity, keep real status above it, and distinguish zero from unavailable data.
Do verify the running native app in Light and Dark Mode, increased contrast, large Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, and Reduced Motion before claiming accessibility approval.
donts: Don't describe a checked, offered, or answered caller as verified, authenticated, or safe.
Don't infer active call checks from stale, missing, paused, or expired status.
Don't promote old tab labels or fixed Surface asset colors from earlier designs into new screens.
Don't present Calls stopped as a lifetime tally, confirmed scams, or evidence that current call checks are on.
Don't treat schematic sidecar HTML/CSS as a native pixel specification.
Don't treat helper access as ownership or extend voicemail access implicitly.
Don't present sample summaries, synthetic speech, or temporary keeping as real-message services.
Don't claim final visual approval, deployment, or real-call evidence from this source extraction.
